blockNote: Actor meta tables: the 7-word world pointer table and the seven lists of 14-byte actor types, 469 entries in all (file offsets 32768-39347, SNES $01:8000-$99B3, bank 00; 6580 bytes).
=== MODEL ===

Every actor placed in a scene, every lair monster and the player is an instance of a meta type: one 14-byte row that gives its stats, first animation, animation table and script. There is one list per world (world_index 0-6: Grass Valley, GreenWood, St. Elles, Mountain of Souls, Leo's Laboratory, Magridd's Castle, World of Evil), so a type number means something different in each world: type $1F is the Metal Mantis in world 0 and a Mini Race Car in world 4. SpawnSceneActors stores the offset of the world's list in $03B0; every consumer reads its row at WorldMetaPointers + $03B0 + type x 14 (listings show $&WorldMetaPointers+N,Y with DBR $01 or $81). The type number comes from a placement row (+3, the PlacementAaaSss lists) or from a lair record (+$15, LairRecords).
=== ENTRY LAYOUT (14 bytes) ===

+0 attack, +1 defence, +2 HP (a binary byte), +3 word EXP (BCD), +5 animation id, +6 word flags (becomes $16; $8000 is added at spawn), +8 word animation table, +A animation bank, +B word script, +D script bank. +8..+A is the 3-byte Address field of structs.json and +B..+D the @Code field. Damage (comments in the combat code): the player's hit on a monster is max(1, attack_current - monster defence (+1)); a monster's hit on the player is attack (+0) - 1 - defense_current, at least 0. The EXP word is added in BCD by KillTarget and drawn as digits by RunEnemyDeath.

HP is binary and EXP is BCD: the bestiary values of docs/walkthrough/enemy-bestiary.md match this reading for every enemy that could be matched (for example Metal Mantis 50 HP and 50 EXP = bytes $32 and $0050).
=== WHAT THE OPERANDS SAY ===

Animation table (+8..+A): 358 of the 469 entries use $7E3800 (the sprite map the scene loader expanded into WRAM: the step lists of ordinary actors travel with the scene), 69 use PaletteAnimLists (bank $0D, the colour animations: mostly types $01-$0F of every list, 14, 14, 13, 15, 5, 3 and 5 types in worlds 0-6; none of the enemies), 7 use PlayerAnims (entry 0 of every world, the hero), 4 use EffectAnims and 31 have $000000 (the actor selects its own table with COP A8). Flags word (+6): $2010 95 times, $2040 87, $0040 49, $0000 43, $2048 39, $2050 38, $1000 22, $3040 21 and 28 more values with fewer entries.

Entry 0 of every list is the hero: attack 1, defence 2, HP 3, animation 0, flags $1180, table PlayerAnims, script InitPlayerActor. The seven copies are identical (the stats are not used; the player's own stats live in the $1B.. fields).
=== ENEMY TYPES (matched by stats) ===

The ROM names nothing. The part notes of the seven lists name the enemy types by matching HP and EXP against the walkthrough bestiary (inferred). Where the bestiary gives several enemies the same stats the ids cannot be told apart this way and the note says so. The four bosses whose ROM HP differs from the bestiary, the world 6 Purple Bull and the types that match no bestiary row are OQ-I033-1 to OQ-I033-4.
=== NOTES ===
- The names MetaGrassValley .. MetaWorldOfEvil label the list starts; a type number is the index of a row inside its list, so type $1F of world 0 is MetaGrassValley + 31 x 14.
- engine_0026F3.code_00296A loads +5 as a word (so the low byte of the flags becomes the high byte of the animation id): harmless for rows whose flags low byte is 0 (OQ-I014-5).

- Consumers: SpawnSceneActors (list offset), InitActorFromPlacement, SpawnLairActor, SpawnLairMonster, RunMonsterAppearPuff, LoadMonsterFromMeta, ApplySwordHit, ApplyProjectileHit, ApplyContactDamageOrPickup, KillTarget, RunEnemyDeath, SetEnemyGauge, HoldActorUntilReleased, FindTalkableActorAt.

blockNote: Scene placement tables: the index of 97 scenes and the 97 actor lists it points to (file offsets 39348-43485, SNES $01:99B4-$A9DD, bank 00; 389 + 3749 bytes).
=== MODEL ===

SpawnSceneActors scans ScenePlacementIndex for the first 4-byte row whose area and scene equal area_current and scene_current (a first byte of $80 or more ends the scan) and hands the row's list to SpawnPlacementList. A scene is one row; the 97 rows are exactly the 97 scenes of the scene profile list (lib_scene_profile_data) and of the asset list (SceneAssetLists, minus its dummy first record).
=== ROWS ===

Index row (4 bytes): +0 area, +1 scene, +2 word &list. List row (4 bytes): +0 x tile, +1 y tile, +2 flags byte (bits 7 and 6 flip Y and X; bit 0 is passed to $1C as $0100), +3 meta type (WorldMetaPointers). Position = x tile x 16, y tile x 16 + 16. A list ends with a byte of $FF. The first row of every list is the hero (meta type 0): its tile is the start position of the scene when no warp_dest is set.

913 rows in all (97 hero rows and 816 actors); the longest list is PlacementA06S01 with 33 rows. The lists are named PlacementAaaSss after the (area, scene) of their index row, both in hex: PlacementA05S02 is area 5, scene 2.
=== AREAS ===

22 areas ($00-$15) with 13, 4, 3, 6, 6, 10, 1, 5, 4, 2, 1, 7, 3, 5, 5, 2, 1, 4, 7, 3, 3 and 2 scenes. docs/areas-and-scenes.md names them and maps (area, scene) to the location_id used by the chest, exit and plate lists.
=== NOTES ===
- Lair monsters are not listed here: they come from LairRecords (the lair actor spawns them), so the 'enemies' of a scene are the placement list plus the lairs of its location.
- structs.json names the index row unk1 and the list row unk2; the 97 lists keep the unk2 type with the delimiter $FF.

blockNote: Chest lists: the 128-word pointer table by location_id and the lists of 6-byte chest rows (file offsets 43486-44181, SNES $01:A9DE-$AC95, bank 00; 256 + 440 bytes).
=== MODEL ===

TryOpenChest (lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) and the scene init code in lib_scene_map_patches read chest_list_ofs, the list of the current location, which the scene loader takes from ChestListPointers[location_id x 2]. A chest is not an actor: the map holds the chest tile ($FB closed, $FC open) and the list says which tile belongs to which chest, what it holds and which bit of the chest array remembers that it was opened.

Row (6 bytes): +0 x, +1 y of the tile the player stands on (the chest tile is one above, y - 1); +2 chest id (bits 0-6 = the bit number in the array $1A7E, bit 7 = the tile is also edited on BG2); +3 content (0 empty, $FF Gems, any other value an inventory entry); +4 word Gem amount (BCD, little-endian: the bytes 12 00 are 12 Gems). A list ends with $FF.
=== WHAT IS HERE ===

97 of the 128 location ids have a list; the 31 ids without a scene (25-27, 35-3B, 48-4F, 5D-63, 74-77, 7E, 7F) hold $0000. Of the 97, 60 share ChestListEmpty (a single $FF byte) and 37 have their own label: 36 with chests (67 chests in all: 1 to 4 per room) and ChestListLoc0A, an empty list of its own (Tulip's Dream) that duplicates the shared one. Names are ChestListLocLL with LL = location_id in hex.

Locations with chests (ROM location names): 03 Treasure room, 05 and 06 the Underground Castle, 08 Leo's Paintings, 0D Trial room, 15 Woods of GreenWood, 16 A mole's hole, 1A-1C Water Shrine, 1D-1F Fire Shrine, 20 Light Shrine, 29 Seabed Sanctuary, 2B Secret Cave, 2E Southerta, 2F Shore reef of Rockbird, 30 Durean, 32 A ghost ship, 34 Seabed of St. Elles, 3E Mountain North slope, 3F Aurora's Ridge, 47 Ice field of Laynole, 51 Leo's Laboratory, 58 the power plant, 5B and 5C Model of a town, 66 the torture chamber, 67 and 68 the castle basement, 6E and 6F the right tower, 79 and 7A World of Evil, 7B Dazzling Space.

Checked against the walkthrough: the chest of the Trial room (ChestListLoc0D) holds item 1, the Sword of Life (01-in-the-beginning.md); the chest in the Underground Castle (ChestListLoc05) holds the 12 Gems of 02-grass-valley.md.
=== NOTES ===
- The bit number is a 7-bit value, so a chest id is below 128; $1A7E lies inside the first switch array ($1A5E + $20) and is the chest-opened array.

blockNote: Exit lists: the 128-word pointer table by location_id and 97 lists of 11-byte exit rows (file offsets 44182-46745, SNES $01:AC96-$B699, bank 00; 256 + 2308 bytes).
=== MODEL ===

CheckExitRegions (lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) runs every frame with exit_list_ofs, the list of the current location, which the scene loader takes from ExitListPointers[location_id x 2]. An exit is a rectangle of tiles; when the player stands inside it (the tile inside, then the pixel position inside the rectangle shrunk by 15 pixels) the scene change starts: area_next, scene_next, warp_dest_anim, warp_dest_x and warp_dest_y are stored and the transition begins. So doors, room edges, ladders and portals are data, not scripts.

Row (11 bytes): +0 x, +1 y, +2 width, +3 height (tiles), +4 area_next, +5 scene_next, +6 warp_dest_anim, +7 word warp_dest_x, +9 word warp_dest_y (pixels). A list ends with $FF. Example: the Trial room list holds one row, x 4, y 10, 1 x 1 tiles, to area 0 scene 1, animation 3, at (96, 96).
=== WHAT IS HERE ===

97 of the 128 ids have a pointer (the 31 without a scene hold $0000, as in the chest table). 78 lists have rows (201 in all; 21 lists have 1 row, 28 have 2, 15 have 3, 5 have 4, 2 have 5, 4 have 6, 2 have 7 and 1 has 11), 18 lists are a single $FF byte and one more (ExitListUnreferenced) is empty and not referenced. Names are ExitListLocLL with LL = location_id in hex.

The 18 empty lists are the places the player leaves by a script, not by walking: the dream rooms (0A Tulip's, 0E Lisa's, 23 Bird's, 24 Stump's, 2D the dolphin's, 33 Servas', 40 the old man's, 43 the mushroom's, 55 the cat's, 69 and 73 the soldier's: 'A dream 1' and the others), the five intro scenes 0F-13, 72 the deck (the Demon Falcon's room) and 7D the battle with Deathtoll.
=== NOTES ===

- Location 5A (the second room the ROM calls 'A dream 1') points at the list of location 56 (ExitListLoc56, two rows to area $0D scene 1 and area $0E scene 2), while the empty list ExitListUnreferenced right after ExitListLoc59 has no reader. Every other dream room has an empty list, so the pointer looks like a slip (OQ-I033-5).
- structs.json declares the exit row as 11 Bytes; +7 and +9 are 16-bit reads (retype proposal in FM-A11 4.17).

blockNote: Plate lists: the 256-word pointer table and 6 lists of 4-byte pressure plate rows, plus the shared empty list (file offsets 46746-47628, SNES $01:B69A-$BA0C, bank 00; 512 + 371 bytes).
=== MODEL ===

A pressure plate is a tile that switches a room between two map variants after a lair was released. TriggerVariantPlate (lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) reads plate_list_ofs, which the scene loader takes from the word at ($03AA = location_id x 4) + plate_variant x 2 of this table; plate_lists_ofs keeps the address of the pair. The index is therefore location_id x 2 + variant (0 or 1): the two lists of a pair are the plates of variant 0 and variant 1, and stepping on an active plate of the current variant applies the lair record's slab and toggles the variant, so the next plate takes over.
Row (4 bytes): +0 x, +1 y of the plate tile, +2 word lair record index (the bit number in the released array $1A9E: the plate is inactive until that lair has been released). A list ends with $FF.
=== WHAT IS HERE ===

Only three rooms have plates: location 01 (Grass Valley, the highlands: PlateListLoc01V0 with 17 rows and PlateListLoc01V1 with 12), location 29 (the Seabed Sanctuary: V0 with 19 rows, V1 with 10) and location 65 (the Castle of King Magridd: V0 with 23 rows, V1 with 10). The rows of one list name only a few lair records (for example PlateListLoc01V0 uses records 2 and 6 in its first rows). 188 of the 256 words point to PlateListEmpty (one $FF byte), 62 are $0000 (the 31 ids without a scene, two words each) and 6 point to the lists above.

blockNote: Lair and release records: 420 records of 32 bytes and a $FF terminator (file offsets 47629-61069, SNES $01:BA0D-$EE8D, bank 00; 13441 bytes). The record index is the switch number of the whole game.
=== MODEL ===

A Monster Lair is a patch of the map ($FD intact, $FE green switch, $FF cleared) that spits out monsters; killing them all opens the switch, and stepping on it releases something: an NPC that goes home (the walkthrough: 'the switch beneath the lair will release the tool shop's owner') or a stretch of map (a path opens). One record describes both halves: where the lair is and what it spawns (+B..+15), and what the release does (+0..+A, +E, +F, +1D, +1E). Record n is also switch n: bit n of the switch array $1ADE and of the released array $1A9E, and byte n of lair_state ($7F0203 + n) is its monster counter. The records are not sorted by location.
=== RECORD (32 bytes) ===

+0 home location (where the released NPC lives; $FF/$80+ ends the table) | +1 slab number (0-3, the alternative map copy shown by the release) | +2, +3 home tile x, y | +4, +5 rectangle x, y (metatiles) | +6, +7 rectangle width, height (0 / 0 writes one type-1 tile) | +8 layer (non-zero: BG2 as well) | +9 name index (the NPC's name in NpcNameStrings) | +A low bits of lair_state after the release ($80 path, $C0 NPC) | +B lair location | +C, +D lair tile x, y (the switch appears here) | +E, +F staging rectangle x, y | +10 word script, +12 script bank (@Code) | +13 monster count (the initial lair_state) | +14 spawn interval (RunLairRespawn, RunLairSpawnAll: $14 = 3 x $26 - 1) or formation index (RunLairFormation: $26 x 2 into FormationPointers) | +15 meta type | +16 word attribute bits ($4000, $8000 or $C000: flips) | +18, +1A words, +1C byte: always 0, no reader | +1D warp_dest_anim | +1E word gate switch (a bit of $1ADE; 0 = none).

The first 8 bytes (+0..+7) are copied by MVN to $1C6D-$1C74 (release_slab, release_npc_x/y, release_rect_x/y/w/h) when a release runs. +E / +F both 0 means the lair frees an NPC; otherwise it opens a path.
=== WHAT IS HERE ===

Scripts: 156 RunLairRespawn, 139 RunLairSpawnAll, 107 RunLairFormation, 8 RunLairProximity, 7 RunLairSpawnAllFlipping and 3 records without a script (monster count 0): records $32, $74 and $75, whose home and lair location is a dream room (0E Lisa's, 23 Bird's, 24 Stump's): switches that no lair actor ever drives.

15 records are identical fillers: home and lair location $63 (a location without a scene), count 1, interval 1, meta type $FF, RunLairRespawn: $26, $27, $2D, $35, $104-$108, $12B, $12C, $146, $156, $157 and $194. Nothing finds them (no scene has location $63), so they only keep the numbering of the switches.

The record index is the switch number everywhere: placement scripts test switch n with COP 14 and COP 3B (HoldActorUntilReleased waits for the lair of record n), and SceneVariantRules names six boss lairs by their index.

Walkthrough check (record $09, the first boss lair): home location 04 (the village chief's room), lair location 0C (Monster in the paintings), lair tile (2, 3), RunLairFormation, 1 monster of meta type $1F (the Metal Mantis, MetaGrassValley). The walkthrough 02-grass-valley.md: 'After beating the Metal Mantis, go onto the northwestern switch that was once underneath the monster lair. You'll end up freeing the village chief'. The other five boss lairs are records $50 (home 15, lair location 22, three Elemental Statues, type $3D), $B6 (home 29, lair 32, Floating Skull, type $41), $103 (home 3D, lair 44, Poseidon, type $38), $12F (home 53, lair 59, Tin Doll, type $1E) and $195 (home 65, lair 72, Demon Falcon, type $09).
Record $00 (home and lair location 0D, the Trial room): 4 monsters of meta type $20, RunLairRespawn.
=== NOTES ===

- Consumers: SpawnLairActor and ApplyLairStatesToScene (spawn and state replay), SealLair, ReleaseLairAtSwitch, PlayLairReleaseScene and RunLairReleaseOnReturn (release), TriggerVariantPlate (plates), HoldActorUntilReleased and Cop3B_JumpIfSwitchSetElseHold (the freed NPCs), InitFixedState (copies +13 to $7F0203 + n).
- structs.json declares unk8 with 16 Bytes, @Code, 3 Bytes and 5 Words; +14 is a byte and +1D a byte read (retype proposal in FM-A11 4.17).
- The existing note of RunLairRespawn says '156 of the 417 lair records': 417 is the number of records that have a script.

blockNote: Lair formations: the 112-word pointer table and 112 lists of 6-byte monster rows (file offsets 61070-63897, SNES $01:EE8E-$F999, bank 00; 224 + 2604 bytes; 434 rows).
=== MODEL ===

RunLairFormation (the script of 107 lair records) places all monsters of a lair at once instead of one after the other. The index is in the lair actor's $26 (the record's +14); the list is the word at FormationPointers + $26 x 2. For each of the lair's monsters (count in $0C, the live count taken from the record's +13) it reads one row: word x, word y, word flip bits (ORed into $1C after AND $3FFF) and spawns the monster at that position with no appear puff.

Rows (6 bytes): +0 word x, +2 word y (pixels), +4 word OR bits for $1C (flip bits $4000 and $8000, so a formation can be mirrored). Lists have no terminator: the monster count ends the walk, so every list must have at least as many rows as the lair has monsters.
=== NOTES ===
- The 112 lists keep their auto names (unk9_00EF6E ...): they are named by index in FormationPointers ($00-$6F), which is what the lair records use.
- Check: 224 + 434 x 6 = 2828 bytes.

blockNote: Scene variant rules: 23 rows of 4 bytes and a terminator (file offsets 63898-63990, SNES $01:F99A-$F9F6, bank 00; 93 bytes).
=== MODEL ===

LookupSceneVariant (lib_scene_map_patches) is called by ApplySceneProfile when scene_variant is still 0. It walks this table for a row of the current location whose switch bit is set in the switch array $1ADE and, if there is one, stores the row's variant in scene_variant ($031E). The variant picks the music of the scene (the music commands of the asset list carry a variant byte).

Row (4 bytes): +0 location_id (a first byte of $80 or more ends the table), +1 word switch number (a bit of $1ADE), +3 variant. The switch numbers are lair record indices (LairRecords): the six values are the boss lairs, one per world: $0009 the Metal Mantis (world 0), $0050 the Elemental Statues (1), $00B6 the Floating Skull (2), $0103 Poseidon (3), $012F the Tin Doll (4) and $0195 the Demon Falcon (5). The record of each switch has the world's boss as its monster (meta type $1F, $3D, $41, $38, $1E, $09).
=== ROWS ===

Rows per world: world 0 locations 01, 02, 03, 04 (variant 2) and 0C (variant 0); world 1 locations 15, 16, 17, 18 (variant 2) and 22 (0); world 2 locations 29, 2C (2) and 32 (0); world 3 locations 3D (2) and 44 (0); world 4 locations 51, 52, 53, 54 (2) and 59 (0); world 5 locations 65 (2), 72 (0) and 71 (1). The variant-0 rows are the six boss rooms, the rooms whose scene profile adds 2 to the variant (byte 11 = $C0-$C5, lib_scene_profile_data): after the boss lair is released the boss room goes back to variant 0 and the other rooms of the world change to variant 2 (the Castle of King Magridd's dock, 71, to variant 1). The story that fits: the boss music of the room before the boss falls and the music of the world after it (inferred; OQ-I011-5). World 6 has no row.
=== NOTES ===

- Bit n of $1ADE is set by the release code (ReleaseLairAtSwitch for a path, PlayLairReleaseScene for an NPC, which runs once the player has returned to the NPC's home scene), so the rooms change after the release, not at the moment the boss dies.

blockNote: Animation bank $0A: the hero's animations without a weapon (file offsets 327680-330951, SNES $0A:8000-$8CC7, bank 05; 3272 bytes).
=== MODEL ===

An animation bank is read through the actor's table pointer ($22, base $8000) and bank ($24): the word list at $8000 holds one pointer per animation id ($1E), each pointing to a step list; the actor's step counter ($20) selects the step, 8 bytes each: word duration, word dx, word dy, word &frame, with $FFFF ending the list (SetActorAnimFrame in engine_scheduler_sprites_combat_collision loads one step per call). A frame is a leaf: a 12-byte header (the box edges, width and height) followed by the sprite map of the pieces. This bank has 26 lists (ids $00-$19), 116 steps and 64 frame leaves. The hero uses it when he has no weapon or the scene has no combat (ApplyPlayerWeaponPose sets $24 = $0A).
The lists are named by index in the pointer table and the leaves by address; they keep their auto names.

partNotes.PlayerUnarmedAnims:
The animation list of the unarmed hero: 26 pointers.

When: the animator reads it for every step of the player actor with $24 = $0A.
Sees: the hero walks and stands without his sword in towns and before he has a weapon.
Why: the animations of an actor are data, not code, so one animator drives every actor.
In: n/a (data): 26 words, index = animation id $1E; each points to a list of 8-byte steps (duration, dx, dy, &frame) ending with $FFFF.
Out: the step and its frame leaf (12-byte header, then the sprite map).
Clobbers: n/a (data).

Same format as bank $0A (data_anim_player_unarmed): a pointer list by animation id, 8-byte steps of duration, dx, dy and &frame, frame leaves with a 12-byte header and a sprite map. This bank has 44 lists (ids $00-$2B), the hero's armed poses: standing, the four walks (six steps of duration 3, dx or dy of 2 pixels per frame in the first step), the crab-walk poses, the sword thrusts and swings and the death. The 44 ids are those of PlayerFacingByAnim. 7 meta entries (entry 0 of every world) point their animation table at it; ApplyPlayerWeaponPose sets $24 = $0B for the armed hero.

blockNote: Animation bank $0D: colour animations, 80 lists of 6-byte copy steps (file offsets 425984-440319, SNES $0D:8000-$B7FF, bank 06; 14336 bytes).
=== MODEL ===

Not sprite animations: the lists are read by the record stepper of lib_animation (COPs 92-95, 9D, 9E) which copies bytes into WRAM bank $7F. A step is 6 bytes: +0 hold count (0 ends the list), +1 word source address (in this bank), +3 destination colour (x 2 = the offset in the CGRAM shadow $7F0000), +4 length - 1, +5 delay. The data fit palette cycling: the source blocks are runs of BGR555 words, and consecutive steps rotate the same colours by one position (for example the leaf at $0680C5 is E749 2B52 8F5E 3273 ..., the next one 2B52 E749 2B52 8F5E ...), written to the same colour index ($71 in that list) every time. Length - 1 is always odd (whole colours) except $02: the 53 steps with destination $00 and 3 bytes ($20 $40 $80 and similar triples) write the three COLDATA bytes of the fixed colour (lib_animation: coldata_buffer at $7F0200), a colour fade of the backdrop.

Destination colours in use include $21, $31, $51, $71, $58, $57, $70, $A1, $91, $81; lengths 3 to 30 bytes (up to 15 colours); hold counts are mostly 1 (614 of 686 steps); delays 0-13 frames. 80 lists, 686 steps, 593 leaves.

69 meta entries (WorldMetaPointers: mostly the types $01-$0F of every world, none of the enemies) use this bank as their animation table, so each is an actor whose 'animation' is a colour cycle; which scene effect each one runs was not traced. FM-A4 and FM-A11 called the lists 'VRAM copy lists'; the destination and the data say colours (OQ-I033-6, a DISCREPANCY with the earlier function map; OQ-I026-3 is the same question seen from the stepper).
The lists are named by index in the pointer table (80 words), the leaves by address; they keep their auto names.

partNotes.PaletteAnimLists:
The colour animation lists: 80 pointers by animation id.

When: the record stepper (lib_animation: NextFrameRecord and CopyFrameData) reads a list step by step for actors with $24 = $0D (69 meta entries).
Sees: colours that rotate through a run of shades and fades of the backdrop colour; which scene effects these are was not traced.
Why: cycling a few palette entries is cheaper than redrawing tiles, so the animation is a list of colour blocks.
In: n/a (data): 80 words, index = animation id $1E; each points to 6-byte steps (hold, &source, destination colour, length - 1, delay) ending with a hold of 0.
Out: the source block (2 to 30 bytes, whole BGR555 colours, or 3 COLDATA bytes) is copied to $7F:offset (destination x 2); $26 = hold - 1, delay to $14 and $0E.
Clobbers: n/a (data).

blockNote: The text dictionary: 128 words of 12 bytes (file offsets 524288-525823, SNES $10:8000-$85FF, bank 08; 1536 bytes).
=== MODEL ===

A string byte of $80 or more is a dictionary word: the text renderers (ExpandDictionaryWord in the menu text, ExpandDialogueWord in dialogue, through ReadTextByte and ReadDialogueByte) print entry (byte and $7F) and a blank. Each entry is 12 bytes, the word padded with zero bytes. The 128 entries are common words (all, and, back, because, ...) and a few names: $0A King, $0B Leo, $0C Liesa, $0D Magridd, $06 Deathtole, $10 Stone. Entries $00-$15 are capitalised, $16-$7F lower case (so $01 is 'A' and $17 'a'); the fragments '-ll', 's', 'm' and 't' ($3F, $57, $46, $65) complete contractions.
ROM spelling against the walkthrough: entry $06 reads 'Deathtole' (OQ-I010-2) and the walkthrough writes 'Deathtoll'; entry $0C reads 'Liesa' and the walkthrough writes 'Lisa' (OQ-I033-7).

partNotes.Dictionary:
The dictionary of 128 common words, 12 bytes each.

When: every string byte of $80 or more in dialogue, menus and item names.
Sees: the word typed out followed by a blank.
Why: dialogue and menu text repeat common words, so each is stored once and referenced by one byte.
In: n/a (data): entry = byte and $7F; 12 bytes: the characters, then zero padding.
Out: up to 12 characters of the entry are drawn.
Clobbers: n/a (data).
